To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of CBI in history instruction in Oregon high schools can help teachers and students meet the state standards, that the use of the concepts in history instruction in this way is a viable alternative to the use of the traditional methods of instruction in history, and that the use of concepts in history instruction can be an effective means of helping teachers meet the requirements of their teaching assignments and the needs of their students.
the CBI program we developed and tested in this research study was successful in improving student learning of history content, history thinking skills, and writing skills.
students in the CBI classes performed significantly better on the state history assessment than did students in the traditional classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of conceptual understanding of history.

the development of a new instructional approach that is based on the premise that the concepts and principles of history should be the focus of instruction, and that students can learn these concepts and principles through the study of history.
the development and evaluation of a curriculum and instruction model that can help teachers meet the challenges they face in helping their students learn history.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CBI is a teaching approach which focuses on the use of concepts and their relationships to develop students’ knowledge and understanding in a specific content area.
the CBI approach to history instruction was successful.
the CBI model was successful in helping the students learn the content, develop the concepts, and develop the critical thinking skills that are necessary for success in the AP U.S. History
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to help teachers and students learn history by using concepts to structure the content and the learning process, and to use those concepts to frame historical thinking.

we are using a concept-based instructional model to help high school students understand the content of the history standards and to develop the skills necessary to use history as a tool to make meaning in their lives (p. 1).
we have developed a model of instruction that is based in the conceptual framework of history.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students are more likely to be engaged and to learn when they are asked to think about the big ideas in the subject matter, rather than just memorize facts.
the concepts we used were powerful enough to serve as the basis for both content and skills instruction.
students need to understand concepts in order to understand the past.
